title: Final room walk-through with a checklist
moduleTitle: Group (Cleaning & Hygiene): Quality, evidence and handover
audience: Cleaners on short-stay, hotel-style and serviced-apartment turnovers who complete the final check on a room before it is released.
learningOutcomes: Walk a finished room in a fixed order, and tick each checklist item as it is checked.
Check the room from the guest's point of view, from the doorway and across the whole room.
Record or fix every item that does not pass, and raise it before the room is released.

instruction.heading: The purpose of the walk-through
instruction.body: The final walk-through checks the finished room the way a guest will first see it. It catches what the earlier stages missed: a dusting point that was skipped, a stray item, a light left on, a bed slightly out of square. It is not a repeat of every task. It is a structured look with a checklist, done once the work is finished and before the room is released. How the release itself is signed off is covered in “Timed guest-ready turnover and final property release”.

instruction.heading: Walking the room in a fixed order
instruction.body: Stand at the entrance and look at the room as a whole first. Then walk round in one direction: the entry and door, the window and curtains, the bed, the bedside table and lamp, the desk or table, the wardrobe and storage, the mini-fridge and kitchen area if present, the bathroom, and the floor last. Hold the checklist and tick each item as you reach it. Do not tick from memory, because memory is what the walk-through is meant to replace.

instruction.heading: What the checklist must cover
instruction.body: A walk-through checklist should cover, at minimum, what this group teaches: no items left by the previous guest; the bed made to standard; surfaces dusted and high-touch points disinfected; the bathroom checked for signs of the previous guest; the restock list complete; the floor finished; the odour and temperature recorded; windows, doors and lights secured or set as the property directs; and no damage left unreported. A business uses its own approved checklist, and this lesson does not replace it.

instruction.heading: Acting on a fault found
instruction.body: If a check fails, fix it if the fault is within your task and tools, and recheck the same item. If it cannot be fixed within your role or the time available, record it and tell the coordinator before the room is released. The walk-through does not end when the first fault is found. It ends when every item is either passed or recorded.

procedure: Stop work, and take your equipment out of the room.
Stand at the entrance and check the room as a whole for stray items and visible marks.
Walk the room in the set order, and tick each checklist item as you reach it.
Check the bed from the door side, and the bathroom from the doorway.
Check that windows, doors and lights are in the positions the property requires.
Fix any fault that is within your scope, and recheck it. Record anything you cannot fix.
Complete the checklist and pass it to the release step in “Timed guest-ready turnover and final property release”.

workedExamples.situation: You have finished a one-bedroom turnover. On the final walk-through you see a dust mark on the base of the lamp near the bed, and the bathroom bin lid is not closed.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the room ready to release?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not yet. Dust the lamp base, close the bin lid, and recheck both spots. The room can move to release once both points pass and the checklist is complete. Any fault you cannot fix is recorded and raised with the coordinator before release.

equipmentAndPpe: Room checklist, in the business's approved version
Torch or other light for corners and under furniture
Clean cloth for final dust and touch checks

commonErrors.error: Walking the room in no particular order and missing a point.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the set order, and tick each item as you reach it.
Check each item in the room before ticking it.

commonErrors.error: Releasing a room with a known fault because release time is close.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the fault and raise it before release. Do not hide it.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the floor edges and the space under furniture.
commonErrors.prevention: Include the floor edges and under-furniture check in the final walk.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Check that windows and doors are secured as the property's procedure requires, and that no equipment, chemicals or tools are left in the room.
Keys, access cards and entry codes are handled under the business's security procedure. This lesson does not authorise anyone to enter or release a property.

qualityStandard: Every checklist item is either passed or recorded before the walk-through ends.
No chemicals, tools or cleaning cloths are left in the room.
Viewed from the doorway, the room meets the standard described in “The hotel room standard and why guests judge cleanliness”.
documentationEvidence: Photos at the points the business requires
Record of any item not passed, with the action taken
summary: The walk-through checks the finished room from the guest's view, using a checklist.
Walk in a fixed order and tick as you go, never from memory.
Fix what is in scope, and record or raise everything else before release.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the main purpose of the final walk-through?
options: To repeat every task so that the room is done twice and the time spent on each task
To check the finished room from the guest's view, with a checklist, before release
To bill the customer for the extra time taken and the cost of the extra products used

knowledgeChecks.question: During a walk-through you find a fault you cannot fix within your role. What do you do?
options: Record it and tell the coordinator before the room is released
Leave it, because release is already close and the coordinator is busy
Move the item out of sight and say nothing to the guest

knowledgeChecks.question: Which order is most useful for a walk-through?
options: The route the worker finds quickest, so the walk-through takes less time
The bathroom first, then everything else
A fixed order around the room, ticking the checklist as you go
